topics.name: 1 · Drug Toxicity and Poisoning
topics.notes: Therapeutic index = TD50/ED50. Margin of safety = LD1/ED99. Toxicity types: dose-dependent, allergic, idiosyncratic, drug-drug interaction. Poisoning care: ABCDE, stop exposure, decontaminate, give the antidote.

questions.q: How is the therapeutic index (TI) computed?
questions.explain: TI = TD50/ED50. With ED50 = 2 and TD50 = 6, TI = 3.

questions.q: Margin of safety is computed as:
questions.explain: It uses ED99 for the desired effect and LD1 for the undesired effect.

questions.q: Drug A has LD1/ED99 = 1 and Drug B has 0.0002. Which is safer?
options: Drug B, because its value is smaller
Drug A, because its margin of safety is larger
questions.explain: A larger margin of safety means a safer drug, so Drug B is much less safe.

questions.q: Which statement about the therapeutic index is true?
options: It compares the toxic dose to the effective dose in 50% of individuals
questions.explain: TI uses TD50 over ED50 from the quantal dose-response curve.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the four types of therapeutic drug toxicity?
questions.explain: The four types are dose-dependent, allergic, idiosyncratic and drug-drug interactions.

questions.q: In dose-dependent reactions, toxicity is proportional to:
options: Drug concentration in the body and duration of exposure
questions.explain: Both concentration and duration of exposure matter.

questions.q: CNS depression from barbiturates (sedation to coma to death) is an example of:
questions.explain: It is dose-dependent: the higher the barbiturate dose, the deeper the depression.

questions.q: Tardive dyskinesia from antipsychotics depends mainly on:
questions.explain: It appears after months to years of use.

questions.q: Which drug class is a classic cause of phototoxicity?
questions.explain: Tetracyclines are the phototoxicity example in the lecture.

questions.q: Which extrapyramidal reaction appears first (hours to 5 days)?
questions.explain: Dystonia: hours to 5 days. Parkinsonism: 5-30 days. Akathisia: 5-60 days. Tardive dyskinesia: months to years.

questions.q: Lip-smacking and worm-like tongue movements are signs of:

questions.q: Compulsive, repetitive motions with agitation describe:

questions.q: The toxic metabolite of acetaminophen that causes hepatocyte necrosis is:
questions.explain: CYP2E1 converts a small fraction of APAP to NAPQI. Glutathione normally detoxifies it.

questions.q: Chemotherapy agents that injure DNA and may cause mutagenic or carcinogenic effects show:
questions.explain: Genotoxic effects come from ionizing radiation, environmental chemicals and chemotherapy.

questions.q: Type I hypersensitivity is mediated by:

questions.q: Hemolytic anemia is an example of which hypersensitivity type?

questions.q: Rash and Stevens-Johnson syndrome are examples of:

options: An abnormal reactivity to a chemical that is peculiar to a given individual

topics.name: 1 · Characteristics of Life
topics.notes: Eight attributes of living things: composition and structure, growth, reproduction, response to stimuli, metabolism, movement, complexity of organization, adaptation.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the eight attributes of living organisms?
questions.explain: The eight: composition and structure, growth, reproduction, response to stimuli, metabolism, movement, complexity of organization, adaptation.

questions.q: In a eukaryotic cell, DNA is kept:
questions.explain: In prokaryotes the DNA floats freely in the cytoplasm.

questions.q: When plant tissue is pierced, it produces what to seal the wound in as little as 5 seconds?
questions.explain: This prevents nutrient loss; plants respond chemically rather than physically.

questions.q: Which are key processes of metabolism?

topics.name: 2 · Chemical Basis of Life
topics.notes: Matter is made of elements and atoms; atomic number = protons; mass number = protons + neutrons. Water is polar (cohesion and adhesion). pH 0-14. First law: energy is constant. Second law: entropy increases. Dehydration synthesis builds polymers; hydrolysis breaks them.

questions.q: Which subatomic particle has no charge?
questions.explain: Protons are positive and electrons negative.

questions.q: The atomic number is the number of:
questions.explain: Mass number = protons + neutrons.

questions.explain: They have the same protons but different mass.

questions.q: The first electron shell holds how many electrons?
questions.explain: The second shell holds 8.

questions.q: Water is a polar molecule because:
options: Oxygen attracts shared electrons more strongly than hydrogen
questions.explain: Oxygen becomes slightly negative and hydrogen slightly positive.
Adhesion is attraction between water and other surfaces. Together they allow capillary action in xylem.

options: Lost electrons and are positively charged
questions.explain: Anions gain electrons and are negative.
0-6 acidic, 7 neutral, 8-14 basic.

questions.q: Each pH unit represents a change in H+ concentration of:
questions.explain: The scale is logarithmic.

questions.q: The first law of thermodynamics states that:
options: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed
questions.explain: Energy in the universe is constant.

questions.q: The second law of thermodynamics says that entropy in isolated systems:
questions.explain: Disorder increases over time.
Potential energy is stored energy.
Exceptions: CO2 and NaHCO3 are classed as inorganic.

topics.notes: Plant cell wall: middle lamella (pectin), primary wall (flexible), secondary wall (lignin). Plasmodesmata connect cells. Know organelle functions and passive and active transport.

questions.q: The main structural component of the plant cell wall is:

questions.q: The middle lamella is made mainly of:

options: Communication between plant cells (sugars, amino acids, ions)
questions.explain: The desmotubule stabilizes the structure.

Lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles

topics.notes: Interphase = G1, S (DNA replication), G2. Mitosis: prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, then cytokinesis. Meiosis I is reductional; meiosis II is equational. Know nondisjunction and chromosomal disorders.
